facts.label: International UAS Exam: English proof

value.text: To be invited to the exam, applicants must prove their English with an internationally recognised test or previous studies.

facts.note: So the plan has the English test result ready by the attachment deadline in late January.

facts.label: Where Bangladeshi applicants apply for the residence permit

value.text: At the Finland Application Centre in New Delhi. Finland has no mission in Bangladesh, and the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi serves Bangladesh. Applicants prove their identity and give fingerprints there, and the permit card is delivered to the same place.

facts.where: Sections: How to apply, Where to apply, and Finland does not have a mission in Bangladesh
facts.note: So the plan adds an Indian visa and a trip to New Delhi.

facts.label: D visa fast track for students

value.text: Students can be issued a D visa when applying for a residence permit for studies, as a fast track.

facts.where: Section: Fast track for holders of a D visa
facts.note: Request it in the same online application as the residence permit, and only if you can travel within two weeks of the decision.

facts.label: Money needed in your account for the residence permit
facts.where: Section on the amount for studies of one year or more
facts.note: 800 EUR for each month, in your own account when you apply, with six months of statements. Money your parents or relatives put into your account is allowed, but Migri may ask where it came from. A sponsorship agreement in place of money in your account is not accepted.

facts.label: Residence permit processing time
facts.note: The University of Helsinki's planning figure, which can be exceeded. Start straight after accepting your place and book the identity appointment first.

facts.label: English bachelor's programmes (University of Helsinki)

value.text: The Bachelor's Programme in Science, and the Bachelor's Programme in Liberal Arts and Sciences.

facts.label: Admission group for school certificates from Bangladesh (University of Helsinki)

value.text: Applicants without the Finnish matriculation examination, IB, EB or a Reifeprüfung or DIA completed in Finland are in admission group 1, on SAT or ACT scores, applying from 5 to 19 January 2027. You cannot choose your group.

facts.where: Section on which admission group you are in
facts.note: The university says its instructions for 2027 will be updated by the end of October 2026, so this is checked again in November.

facts.label: SAT scores in 2025, Bachelor's Programme in Science (University of Helsinki)

value.text: In spring 2025 the SAT group had 276 applicants and 73 were accepted. The minimum score, set by the Dean, was 1480.

facts.note: A past year's figure, shown so you can judge how competitive the programme is.

facts.label: Admission for applicants with A levels or HSC (Aalto)

value.text: A levels and other school certificates from outside Finland are in admission round A, on SAT or ACT scores only. They cannot be considered in certificate-based admission.

facts.label: SAT and ACT minimums (Aalto)

value.text: Economics, Finance and International Business: an SAT total of at least 1200, or an ACT composite of 25. Science and Technology, and Technology, Business and Design: an SAT total of at least 1350 with at least 700 in Math, or an ACT composite of 29 with at least 30 in Math. Only tests taken on or after 1 January 2025 count.

facts.where: Section on SAT and ACT requirements

facts.label: English bachelor's programmes (Aalto)

value.text: Economics; Finance; International Business at the Mikkeli campus; Science and Technology, with options in chemical engineering, computer engineering, data science, digital systems and design, mechanical and civil engineering, and quantum technology; and Technology, Business and Design.

facts.label: SAT requirement, Information and Communication Technology (University of Turku)

value.text: Applicants with HSC or A levels apply in group I with the SAT. The minimum is 1150 in total and 600 in Math, and the result may be no more than two years old.

facts.label: English bachelor's programmes (University of Turku)

value.text: Information and Communication Technology, and Sustainable and Social Entrepreneurship.

facts.label: Admission group for applicants with HSC or A levels (Tampere University)

value.text: Applicants with school certificates from outside Finland apply in group I, with SAT or ACT scores. Group II is for the Finnish matriculation examination, and IB, EB and RP/DIA completed in Finland. Superscores are not accepted.

facts.where: Sections on admission groups and SAT scores

facts.label: Which SAT sittings count (Tampere University)

value.text: Only SAT or ACT tests taken after 1 January 2025 count, and the December 2026 test date is the last one for the January 2027 application.

facts.label: Lowest SAT scores admitted in 2026 (Tampere University)

value.text: In 2026, the lowest SAT scores admitted in group I included 1210 in Administrative Sciences and in Technology, and 1250 in Social Sciences. Some programmes combined the SAT with a video.

facts.note: A past year's figure, shown so you can judge how competitive the programmes are.

facts.label: English bachelor's programmes (Tampere University)

value.text: Eleven programmes: six in Science and Engineering (Automation and Robotics, Biomedical Engineering, Chemistry, Engineering Physics, Environmental Engineering, and Materials Science), Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering, three on Sustainable Urban Development (Administrative Sciences, Social Sciences, and Technology), and Socially Sustainable Societies.

facts.label: Admission for applicants with HSC or A levels (University of Oulu)

value.text: The three technology programmes accept the SAT only, not the ACT. International Business Management accepts both SAT and ACT results.

facts.label: English bachelor's programmes (University of Oulu)

value.text: Computer Science and Engineering; Electronics and Communications Engineering; Software Engineering and Information Systems; and International Business Management.

facts.label: English bachelor's programmes (University of Jyväskylä)

value.text: Business Innovation and Sustainability; Immersive Software Engineering and Artificial Intelligence; and Early Childhood Education (EarlyEdu), taught in English with Finnish built into the programme.

facts.note: EarlyEdu qualifies students to work as early childhood education teachers in Finland. The university says the Finnish level needed for that work cannot be guaranteed by the end of the studies.

facts.label: English bachelor's programmes (LUT)

value.text: Fifteen programmes: thirteen in engineering and technology, including software, energy, electrical, mechanical, chemical and civil engineering and computational science, four of them double degrees with Hebei University of Technology, and two in business.

facts.label: Rolling admission (LUT)

values.note: Places go to applicants who meet every requirement, while places remain. Results come within a month of a complete application.
Expected to run from September to April, as for 2027 entry. Month only.

facts.label: Admission with HSC or other national certificates (LUT)

value.text: Your school certificate must give university eligibility in your home country and be completed by 31 August 2027. Then meet either LUT's grade requirements or its maths test or SAT requirement. Business: an overall grade average of 80% and 70% in standard maths. Technology: an overall average of 70%, 80% in advanced maths (90% for Computational Science and Artificial Intelligence) and 80% in physics or chemistry depending on the programme; or 60% in LUT's online maths test. Both: or an SAT of 1300 with at least 600 in Reading and Writing and 700 in Math, or an ACT of 28 with 30 in Math.

facts.note: LUT's tables are labelled 2026 entry requirements and may change for 2027 entry.

facts.label: Admission with A levels (LUT)

value.text: At least three A levels at BBC. Technology needs maths at C or better and a pass in physics or chemistry, depending on the programme. Business needs maths at C at A level or B at AS level. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are accepted.

facts.note: LUT's tables are labelled 2026 entry requirements and may change for 2027 entry.

facts.label: English requirement (LUT)

value.text: IELTS Academic 6.5 with at least 6.0 in writing and speaking; TOEFL iBT 4.5 with 4 in writing and speaking (90 with 22 on the old scale); or PTE Academic 62 with 54 in writing and speaking. A level students with GCSE English at grade C as a first language, or B as a second language, need no test.

facts.note: The GCSE rule is on LUT's page for A level applicants.

facts.label: Entrance exam route, Social Sciences (University of Eastern Finland)

value.text: Apply from 7 to 21 January 2027. Selection is by an online entrance exam with written and video tasks, taken between 8 March and 9 April 2027, and a compulsory online interview. No SAT is needed. 25 places are filled this way.

facts.label: SAT requirement, Data Engineering (University of Eastern Finland)

value.text: The SAT group needs a total of at least 1250 and at least 650 in Math, together with a video.

facts.label: English bachelor's programmes (University of Eastern Finland)

value.text: Eight programmes, including Data Engineering, Information Technology, Social Sciences, Human and Planetary Health, and Sustainable Forest Bioeconomy.

facts.label: Language of bachelor's programmes (Åbo Akademi)

value.text: All bachelor's programmes at Åbo Akademi are taught in Swedish, and applicants must prove sufficient Swedish. Applications run from 9 to 23 March 2027.

facts.label: English requirement (University of Helsinki)

value.text: IELTS Academic 6.5 with at least 6.0 in every section, TOEFL iBT 4.5 with at least 4 in every section (92 on the old scale), PTE Academic 68, or Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency. An SAT score of at least 550 in Evidence-Based Reading and Writing also counts. Schooling in English counts only in the Nordic countries, Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK and the USA.

facts.where: Lists of accepted tests and previous education
facts.note: Test results are valid for two years and must stay valid while the application is processed.

facts.label: English requirement (Aalto)

value.text: Applicants are expected to have English good enough to study in it, and are not required to submit a language test result.

facts.label: English requirement, SAT applicants (University of Turku)

value.text: Applicants selected through the SAT do not have to provide a separate certificate of English.

facts.label: English requirement (Tampere University)

value.text: Applicants admitted on SAT or ACT scores in group I need no further proof of English. The tests accepted otherwise include IELTS Academic 6.0 with at least 5.5 in writing, TOEFL iBT 4 with no section below 3.5 (78 on the old scale), and PTE Academic 62 with at least 61 in writing.

facts.where: Sections on SAT and ACT and on language tests

facts.label: English requirement (University of Jyväskylä)

value.text: In Business Innovation and Sustainability, a qualifying SAT or ACT score also proves English. The tests accepted otherwise include IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5, TOEFL iBT 4 with no section below 3.5, and PTE Academic 62 with at least 61 in writing. In Immersive Software Engineering and Artificial Intelligence, English is assessed only in the programme's own assessment.

facts.label: English requirement (University of Oulu)

value.text: SAT and ACT results are one of the accepted ways to prove English. The tests accepted include IELTS 6.0 with at least 5.5 in each section, TOEFL iBT 4.0 with at least 3.5 in each section, and PTE Academic 62 with at least 61 in writing.

facts.label: English requirement (University of Eastern Finland)

value.text: IELTS Academic 6.0 with at least 5.5 in every part, TOEFL iBT 4 with no part below 3.5, or PTE Academic 62 with at least 61 in writing. SAT scores also prove English only in Data Engineering and in Human and Planetary Health.

facts.label: Scholarships for English bachelor's students (University of Helsinki)

value.text: There are no tuition fee waivers for English bachelor's degrees. Second and third year students may receive a Dean's award of 1,000 EUR for strong study results.

facts.label: Scholarships and discounts (Aalto)

value.text: The competitive Aalto University Excellence Scholarship covers the full tuition fee for the three years of a bachelor's degree, but not living costs, and is applied for in the admission application form. Without it, students who accept their place and pay within 21 days receive 25% off the first year's fee.

facts.label: Scholarships for students admitted from 2026 (University of Turku)

value.text: No first-year scholarship. A 50% scholarship for the second and third years goes to every student who completes 55 credits in the first year (110 after two years) with an average grade of at least 3 out of 5, and at least 4 credits of Finnish.

facts.label: Scholarships and discounts (Tampere University)

value.text: A selective scholarship covers 50% of tuition for the whole programme and is applied for in the same Studyinfo application as admission. Not every programme offers it, and only nine were awarded in 2026 across all bachelor's and master's programmes. Without it, accepting and paying within 21 days takes 2,000 EUR off the first year.

facts.label: Scholarships (University of Oulu)

value.text: From the second year, a 30% fee waiver in the three technology programmes (7,000 EUR a year) and 20% in International Business Management (8,000 EUR). Oulu also has a first-year early bird discount, whose amount is on its page.

facts.label: Scholarships and discounts (University of Jyväskylä)

value.text: No first-year scholarship, and no fully funded scholarships. Accepting within 14 days takes 1,500 EUR off the first year. For the second and third years, students who complete at least 55 credits a year can apply for 3,000 EUR off a 10,000 EUR fee, or 6,000 EUR off a 16,000 EUR fee.

facts.label: Scholarships and discounts (LUT)

value.text: An early bird discount of 2,000 EUR off the first year, except in the double-degree programmes. 3,000 EUR for the second year after at least 60 credits in the first year, and 3,000 EUR for the third year after at least 120 credits.

facts.label: Scholarships and discounts (University of Eastern Finland)

value.text: Paying within 21 days of the result takes 30% off the first year. For the second and third years, a 30% waiver after at least 55 credits in the first year, applied for separately. A one-time Finnish award of 2,500 EUR for a Finnish language certificate, or 1,500 EUR for Finnish studies completed at the university.

facts.note: The university says the waiver values change from the 2027 to 2028 academic year.

facts.label: Discounts and scholarships (Metropolia University of Applied Sciences)

value.text: An early bird discount of 1,000 EUR for students who accept within 14 days and pay on time. Later scholarships depend on passing a Finnish language test.

facts.label: Discounts and scholarships (Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences)

value.text: An early bird discount of 2,000 EUR off the first year. Later scholarships of 2,000 EUR or 3,500 EUR need a passed Finnish YKI test at level 2 or 3 and at least 60 or 120 credits.

facts.label: Scholarships (Tampere University of Applied Sciences)

value.text: A 50% waiver for the first year for students who accept within 14 days and pay the first instalment. Later, 25% for 60 credits a year, or 50% for 60 credits and a Finnish YKI result.

facts.label: Discounts and scholarships (Turku University of Applied Sciences)

value.text: An early bird discount of 1,000 EUR for students who accept within 14 days and pay within 30. A Finnish language scholarship of 4,000 EUR, awarded in stages as you pass YKI tests at levels 2, 3 and 4.

facts.note: The page does not say whether the 4,000 EUR is the total or the amount for each stage.

facts.label: Finnish government scholarships for bachelor's study

value.text: There are no Finnish government scholarships for bachelor's or master's studies. Posts claiming fully funded government scholarships are misleading.

facts.label: Universities and universities of applied sciences

value.text: Universities focus on academic learning and scientific research. Universities of applied sciences focus on practical, career-oriented study.

facts.where: Answer on the two kinds of institution

facts.label: Length of a bachelor's degree at a university of applied sciences

value.text: 210, 240 or 270 credits, with a recommended length of 3.5 to 4.5 years. Practical training is part of the degree. Finland has 24 universities of applied sciences.

facts.label: Length of a bachelor's degree (Aalto)

value.text: A bachelor's degree is three years of full-time study.

facts.where: Section on the Excellence Scholarship and the normative study period

facts.label: Master's study after a degree from a university of applied sciences

value.text: A bachelor's degree from a university of applied sciences is equivalent to a university bachelor's degree. A master's degree at a university of applied sciences needs two years of work experience after the bachelor's.

facts.label: Tuition for programmes taught in Finnish or Swedish

value.text: Under Finland's Universities Act, tuition fees apply to bachelor's and master's programmes taught in a language other than Finnish or Swedish. A student whose language of study changes to Finnish or Swedish no longer pays them.

facts.label: Finnish needed for a Finnish-taught degree (University of Turku)

value.text: Applicants whose schooling was not in Finnish need level 4 in every part of the Finnish YKI test, or the state language exam at the good level.

facts.label: HSC for universities of applied sciences

value.text: The Higher Secondary Certificate, the Alim certificate and the BTEB Diploma in Engineering give eligibility. Send the certificate and the mark sheet or transcript.

facts.note: The shared eligibility list of Centria, Jamk, Oamk, SeAMK, TAMK and Xamk. Haaga-Helia's list says the same.

facts.label: A levels for universities of applied sciences

value.text: At least 2 A level subjects with a pass, or at least 4 AS levels.

facts.label: English tests for universities of applied sciences

value.text: IELTS Academic 6.0, TOEFL iBT 3.5 on the new scale (60 on the old), PTE Academic 55, a Cambridge English Scale score of 169, TELC B2-C1 or Oxford ELLT 6.0. The Duolingo English Test is not accepted. Schooling in Bangladesh, including A levels taken there, does not count as previous study in English.

facts.where: Accepted tests and the list of countries for previous studies

facts.label: International UAS Exam: format

value.text: Taken online on your own computer, not a phone, under remote supervision. Every applicant sits reasoning and English sections, most fields add maths, technology adds advanced maths and physics, and health and social fields add short ethical and emotional intelligence sections. You must pass every section.

facts.label: How many programmes you can apply to

value.text: You can apply to up to six programmes with one application form, and you can be offered more than one study place.

facts.note: You may accept only one of the places offered.

facts.label: Accepting a study place

value.text: You may accept only one study place leading to a degree, starting in the same term, anywhere in Finnish higher education.

facts.label: Paying the application fee

value.text: A payment link arrives by email after you apply, and you have seven days to pay. If you do not pay, your application is not processed. One payment covers every application for studies starting in the same term.

facts.label: The autumn joint application, for studies starting in January

value.text: A second joint application in autumn, for studies starting in January, has a limited number of English-taught programmes. In 2026 it ran from 31 August to 10 September.

facts.where: Section on the autumn joint application

facts.label: Bangladeshi students admitted in 2026

value.text: In the first joint application of spring 2026, 8% of the applicants offered a place were from Bangladesh. After Finns, only Pakistanis, at 9%, were a larger group.

facts.label: Tuition money for the residence permit

value.text: If your tuition fee is not yet paid, the money for it must also be in your bank account when you apply, on top of the living money. If it is paid or waived, attach the proof.

facts.label: Health insurance for the residence permit

value.text: For studies of two years or more, insurance covering medicine costs up to at least 40,000 EUR. For shorter studies, insurance covering medical costs up to at least 120,000 EUR. The excess may be at most 300 EUR, and ordinary travel insurance is not accepted.

facts.label: How fast student permits are decided

value.text: Student applications are handled as urgent. In May 2026, about 61% of first residence permits for studies were decided within 30 days.

facts.label: Service fee at the Finland Application Centre in New Delhi
facts.note: Paid on top of Migri's fee, in Indian rupees.

facts.label: Verification of Bangladeshi civil documents

value.text: Since 3 November 2025, Bangladeshi birth, marriage and similar civil documents must be verified through VFS in New Delhi before the Embassy of Finland legalises them. It mainly affects family members' applications.

facts.label: How long the student residence permit lasts

value.text: Degree students can be granted a continuous permit for the whole length of their studies. Money is shown for the first year, but you must be able to support yourself throughout.

facts.label: Working while you study in Finland

value.text: Paid work in any field for an average of 30 hours a week, 1,560 hours a year. Training and thesis work that is part of the degree is not limited.

facts.label: Finding part-time work in Finland

value.text: Finding part-time work can be challenging, particularly without Finnish or Swedish skills. You should not rely on employment to finance your studies.

facts.label: Looking for work after graduating in Finland

value.text: A residence permit to look for work or start a business, for up to two years, applied for within five years of the student permit ending. You need 800 EUR for each month.

facts.label: Registering as a resident

value.text: To get a Finnish personal identity code and a municipality of residence, you apply online and usually also visit the Digital and Population Data Services Agency in person.

facts.label: Student healthcare fee per term in 2026
facts.note: Paid to Kela each term by degree students at universities and universities of applied sciences. The fee is confirmed for each calendar year, and the 2027 rate was not yet published on 21 October 2026.

facts.label: Social security for international students

value.text: Students who come to Finland to study usually cannot get Kela benefits. Students on degrees of two years or more may receive some benefits, but not general housing allowance.

facts.label: Living costs for a student (University of Helsinki)

value.text: In Helsinki, monthly living costs for a student are 1,000 to 1,300 EUR or more. Student housing costs 450 to 800 EUR a month. The university says living on 9,600 EUR a year in Helsinki will be very tight.

facts.label: Fake Finnish universities

value.text: Kestora University, Penkka University and Heffring University do not exist. A university or programme not listed on Study in Finland, Studyinfo or the Ministry of Education and Culture's site is not officially recognised.

facts.label: Fake job offers in Finland

value.text: Finnish companies do not charge fees for job offers, and a recruitment agency cannot give you a work permit. Only the Finnish Immigration Service charges the official application fees.

facts.label: Agents who paint a misleading picture

value.text: Yle reported that agents working as partners of Finnish institutions told international students that part-time work was easy to find and would cover their living costs. Many struggled to make ends meet, and some took out large loans to come.

facts.label: Fake calls from the immigration service

value.text: Migri never asks for online banking codes by phone. Scammers call pretending to be from Migri. Type migri.fi into your browser yourself.

facts.label: Tuition fees from autumn 2026

value.text: From autumn 2026, tuition fees that cover the institutions' full costs are charged in full.

facts.label: Social assistance and the student permit

value.text: The government has proposed that, as a rule, a student who receives social assistance has their residence permit cancelled or not renewed. It was planned to take effect in October or November 2026 if Parliament approves.

facts.note: Still pending on 21 October 2026. Checked again in November.

facts.label: Family members of students

value.text: The government decided that a student's family members may move to Finland only one year after the student, and outlined a requirement for sufficient skill in the language of instruction for the study permit.

facts.note: Decided on 18 December 2025. Not law yet: see the next fact for the bill.

facts.label: Selection, Immersive Software Engineering and Artificial Intelligence (University of Jyväskylä)

value.text: An online admission test on 10 and 11 February 2027, then online interviews from 17 to 24 March 2027. Results by 8 April 2027.

facts.note: The university says an SAT result may be needed depending on your previous qualification, so check the programme's admission criteria.

facts.label: Final diploma for students finishing school in 2027 (Aalto)

value.text: By 29 January 2027, a certificate of ongoing studies or your latest transcript. The final diploma by 31 July 2027 at 15:00 Finnish time.

facts.where: Timeline for qualifications completed outside Finland in spring 2027

facts.label: Final certificates for conditionally admitted students (University of Turku)

value.text: Conditionally admitted applicants must submit their final certificates by 15 August 2027.

facts.label: Final certificates for students finishing school in 2027 (Tampere University)

value.text: Confirmation of graduation and officially certified documents by 23 August 2027 at 15:00 Finnish time. Your school education must be completed before your studies begin.

facts.label: Final certificate deadline in 2026 (Laurea)

value.text: Students who finished school in spring 2026 had to submit their final certificate by 9 July 2026. Laurea may withdraw a study place if certificates do not arrive in time.

facts.note: Laurea had not yet published its 2027 date. Other universities of applied sciences set their own.

facts.label: Refund of the residence permit fee

value.text: The fee will not be refunded, even if you cancel your application or it is rejected.

facts.label: Application rounds, International Business Management (University of Oulu)

value.text: In the January joint application, International Business Management has one certificate-based group. It also has a rolling admission in October on SAT or ACT scores.

facts.note: Oulu's page did not give the October 2026 dates in a readable form.

facts.label: Credits in a year of study

value.text: One full year of studies is equivalent to 60 credits.

facts.label: Separate application on test scores (Metropolia)

value.text: Metropolia also selects on SAT, ACT, GMAT or GRE scores in its separate application for international degree programmes.

facts.where: Section on who the fees apply to

facts.label: Preliminary assignment, Technology, Business and Design (Aalto)

value.text: Instructions are published on 17 December 2026, and the assignment is due by 22 January 2027 at 15:00 Finnish time. Applicants who pass it are ranked on their SAT or ACT scores.

facts.label: Registration events for new students

value.text: International higher education students should first use the agency's registration events, which are mainly organised with universities.

facts.label: The bill on students' families and language skills

value.text: A bill was submitted to Parliament on 10 September 2026. The one-year wait for family members is planned to apply from 5 April 2027, and the other changes, including a language requirement for student permits, from October 2027.

facts.note: Yle's report. The government's own release could not be read.
